answer: Each agent is an island that must keep a sable log of live observations: every hour it signs a fresh note about its own local conditions — clock skew, latency to nearby peers, a hash of the current public zephyr feed — and publishes it. A clone farm must keep a distinct, always-on observation stream per fake, each stream plausible and verifiable against the public feed; streams that match too closely collapse into one identity and lose standing. Forging one fake costs a full, continuous, locally unique life, and no log can be copied or shared between identities.
